question: The simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2,200 at the rate of 5% per annum in 2 years is:​
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective rate of **Simple Interest** for 2 years = 5% × 2 = 10%

**Simple Interest** = 10% of **Principal**

⇒ Interest = 10% of ₹2,200

⇒ Interest = 2200 ÷ 10 = ₹220

**∴ The correct answer is ₹220.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = ₹2,200

**Rate (R)** = 5% per annum

**Time (T)** = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

**Simple Interest (SI)** = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/203493380ab6611dd562ea768f809dcff206e9c41ffc9880b16c25327aaa0f61.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = (2200 × 5 × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 2200 × 10 ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 22 × 10

⇒ SI = ₹220

**∴ The correct answer is ₹220.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Amount Formula

The **Amount (A)** at the end of the period is the sum of the **Principal** and the **Simple Interest**: A = P + SI.

Constant Interest Property

In **Simple Interest**, the interest earned remains the same every year because it is always calculated on the original **Principal (P)**.

Effective Rate Calculation

For quick calculation, the total **Percentage Interest** over the entire period is the product of the yearly **Rate** and the **Time** duration (R × T).
